bands.1:
The Soggy Biscuit sails into Scaffold Peaks. Snow is falling. Tall rock towers rise out of the sea. Ladders and rope bridges join them up.

"Ninety-nine per cent of this island is up," says Tully. "The rest is falling."

A line of Queuepillars marches along a pole, nose to tail.

Mo makes pickled-onion porridge. It crunches.

"Why are mountains so funny?" asks Mo. "They're hill-arious!"

Everyone groans. A Chorrawong copies them. "Groan! Groan!"

On the tallest tower are gold cranes. A sign says, "MAXX WORLD! THE HAPPIEST SANCTUARY ON EARTH!"

A rock-wallaby hops down a ladder. He wears a tiny yellow hard hat. Behind him, a woman slides down a rope. She lands on your deck.

"I will say three things," she says. "First, hello. Second, this is my island. Third, who are you? In conclusion, explain yourselves."

"Um, Maxx, and the map, and a net, and then..." says Zed.

The wallaby thumps his foot.

"That does not hang together," says the woman. "Say your main point first."

"Maxx is stealing Creatures," says Zed.

"Better," she says. "I am the Architect. I built these ladders for the Creatures. This is Girderoo. He thumps when things are out of order."

"Maxx asked me to plan his sanctuary," she says. "Then he locked me out." The gate says, "NO ARCHITECTS."

"He won't come up here himself," says Wren. "He hates the cold. He sends drones."

The Architect looks hard at her. "Lucky guess," says Wren.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"First, win my badge," says the Architect. "Second, we talk. In conclusion, not yet."

Girderoo hops up to the fence to look.

A gold drone hums down. Maxx's voice comes out of it.

"A wallaby in a hard hat? That's Maxx-imum content! Bag him!"

A net drops. Girderoo is gone.

For the first time, the Architect's words come out in a jumble.

"Girderoo... net... my wallaby."
bands.2:
The Soggy Biscuit sails into Scaffold Peaks through swirling snow. The island is a crowd of rock towers rising out of the sea, like a giant's stack of grey blocks. Wooden scaffolds, ladders and rope bridges join the towers together, creaking in the icy wind.

"Statistically," says Tully, "ninety-nine per cent of this island is up. The other one per cent is falling."

The Creatures here all know exactly where they're going. A line of Queuepillars marches along a scaffold pole, nose to tail.

Mo serves pickled-onion porridge. It crunches.

"Why are mountains so funny?" asks Mo. "Because they're hill-arious!"

Everyone groans. A Chorrawong on the next tower copies them and calls it across the valley: "Groan! Groan! GROAN!"

On the tallest tower, gold cranes swing above a gold fence. A huge billboard says, "MAXX WORLD! THE HAPPIEST CREATURE SANCTUARY ON EARTH! OPENING SOON!"

Then a rock-wallaby in a tiny yellow hard hat bounds down a ladder towards you. Behind him, a woman in an orange hi-vis vest slides down a rope and lands on your deck with a thud.

"I will say three things," she announces. "First, good morning. Second, this is my island. Third, who are you? In conclusion, explain yourselves."

"Um, so, there's Maxx," says Zed, "and then the map, but first a net, and also our boat leaks, and..."

The wallaby thumps his foot, hard.

"That does not hang together," says the woman. "Start with your main point. Then your reasons."

Zed takes a breath. "Maxx is stealing Creatures. We're here to set them free."

"Better," she says. "I am the Architect. I built every scaffold on these peaks. This is Girderoo. He thumps when things are in the wrong order."

She glares up at the gold fence. "Maxx hired me to plan his sanctuary. First, he praised my drawings. Second, he took them. Third, he locked me out." A sign on the gate says, "NO ARCHITECTS."

"He won't come up here himself," says Wren. "He hates the cold. He sends drones."

The Architect looks hard at her. Wren shrugs. "Lucky guess."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"First, win my badge," says the Architect. "Second, then we'll talk. In conclusion, not yet."

Just then, Girderoo bounds up the scaffold to peek through the gold fence.

A gold drone hums out of the clouds above him, and Maxx's voice crackles from its speaker.

"A wallaby in a hard hat? He's already dressed for Maxx World! That's Maxx-imum content. Bag him!"

A net drops. Girderoo is gone.

For the first time, the Architect's words come out in no order at all.

"Girderoo... the net... they... my wallaby."
bands.3:
The Soggy Biscuit sails into Scaffold Peaks through a swirl of snow. The island is nothing but rock towers, dozens of them, rising out of the sea like a giant's stack of grey blocks. Between the towers, a web of wooden scaffolds, ladders and rope bridges creaks and sways in the icy wind.

"Statistically," says Tully, through chattering teeth, "ninety-nine per cent of this island is up. The other one per cent is falling."

Gus sneezes. The boat springs a leak, and the water freezes into a slippery puddle that Zed immediately falls over in.

The Creatures here all seem to know exactly where they're going. A line of Queuepillars marches along a scaffold pole, nose to tail. A Heddrake suns itself on the top rock of a tower, and wherever its head points, its long tail follows.

Mo serves breakfast: pickled-onion porridge, lumpy and steaming and somehow crunchy. "It warms you from the inside," he says. Nobody tests this.

"Why are mountains so funny?" asks Mo. "Because they're hill-arious!"

The groan is so loud that a Chorrawong on the next tower picks it up and calls it across the valley. "Groan! Groan! GROAN!" Soon the whole island is groaning at Mo.

On the tallest tower of all, gold cranes swing above a gold fence. A billboard blazes through the snow: "MAXX WORLD! THE HAPPIEST CREATURE SANCTUARY ON EARTH! OPENING SOON!" Goldies in gold hard hats scurry along the scaffolds with long, flat boxes.

Then a rock-wallaby in a tiny yellow hard hat bounds down a ladder towards you, three rungs at a time. Behind him, a woman abseils down the rock and lands on your deck with a thud. She wears an orange hi-vis vest, a tape measure on her belt and a rolled-up blueprint under one arm.

"I will say three things," she announces. "First, good morning. Second, this is my island. Third, who are you? In conclusion, explain yourselves."

"Um, so, there's Maxx," Zed begins, "and then the map, but first there was a net, and also our boat leaks, and..."

The wallaby thumps his foot on the deck, hard.

"That does not hang together," says the woman. "Start with your main point. Then your reasons. Then stop."

Zed takes a breath. "Maxx is stealing Creatures. We've seen his nets. We're here to break them out."

"Better," she says. "I am the Architect. I built every scaffold on these peaks, so the Creatures could travel between the towers. This is Girderoo. He thumps when things are in the wrong order, which is often."

The Architect glares up at the gold fence. "Maxx hired me to design his sanctuary. First, he praised my drawings. Second, he took them away. Third, he locked me out." She points at a sign on the gate: "NO ARCHITECTS."

"He won't come up here to look at it himself," says Wren. "He hates the cold. He sends drones."

The Architect looks hard at her. Wren shrugs. "Lucky guess."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"First, win my badge," says the Architect. "Second, then we will talk. In conclusion, not yet."

Just then, Girderoo pricks up his ears and bounds up the scaffold to peek through the gold fence.

A gold MaxxCam drone hums out of the clouds above him, and Maxx's voice crackles from its speaker.

"A wallaby in a hard hat? He's already dressed for Maxx World! That's Maxx-imum content, Vantafam. Bag him!"

A net drops. Girderoo is gone before anyone can move.

The Architect opens her mouth. For the first time, her words come out in no order at all.

"Girderoo... the net... they... my wallaby."
bands.4:
The Soggy Biscuit sails into Scaffold Peaks through a swirl of snow, towards an island that is nothing but rock towers, dozens of them, rising out of the sea like a giant's stack of grey building blocks. Between the towers, a web of wooden scaffolds, ladders and rope bridges creaks and sways in the icy wind.

"Statistically," says Tully, through chattering teeth, "ninety-nine per cent of this island is up. The other one per cent is falling."

Gus sneezes. The boat springs a leak, and the water freezes into a small, slippery puddle that Zed immediately falls over in.

The Creatures here all seem to know exactly where they are going. A line of Queuepillars marches nose to tail along a scaffold pole, each caterpillar following the one in front. A Heddrake suns itself on the very top rock of a tower, and wherever its head points, its long tail follows. A Ledgeling darts past with a beak full of mud, building a fresh nest on a brand-new ledge.

Mo serves breakfast: pickled-onion porridge, lumpy and steaming and somehow crunchy. "It warms you from the inside," he says. Nobody is willing to test this.

"Why are mountains so funny?" asks Mo. "Because they're hill-arious!"

The groan is so loud that a Chorrawong on the next tower picks up the word and calls it across the valley. "Groan! Groan! GROAN!" Soon the whole island is groaning at Mo.

On the tallest tower of all, gold cranes swing above a gold fence. A billboard the size of a tennis court blazes through the snow: "MAXX WORLD! THE HAPPIEST CREATURE SANCTUARY ON EARTH! OPENING SOON!" Goldies in gold tracksuits and gold hard hats scurry along the scaffolds, carrying long, flat boxes stamped "HAPPY HOME (FLAT PACK)". The boxes are exactly the size of a small cage.

Then something bounds down the scaffold towards you, three rungs at a time. It's a rock-wallaby wearing a tiny yellow hard hat. Behind it, a woman abseils down the rock in a single smooth drop and lands on your deck with a thud. She wears an orange hi-vis vest over a puffer jacket, a tape measure on her belt and a rolled-up blueprint under one arm.

"I will say three things," she announces. "First, good morning. Second, this is my island. Third, who are you? In conclusion, explain yourselves."

"Um, so, there's Maxx," Zed begins, "and then the map, but first there was a net, and also we've got a boat, which leaks, and..."

The wallaby thumps his foot on the deck, hard.

"That does not hang together," says the woman. "Start with your main point. Then give your reasons. Then stop."

Zed takes a deep breath. "Maxx is stealing Creatures. We've seen his nets. We're here to break them out."

"Better," she says. "I am the Architect. I built every scaffold on these peaks, so the Creatures could travel safely between the towers. This is Girderoo. He thumps when things are in the wrong order, which is often."

Girderoo hops to a pile of pebbles, stacks them neatly from biggest to smallest, then looks up at you as if to say, "Like that."

The Architect stares up at the gold fence. When she speaks again, she is measuring every word. "Maxx hired me to design his sanctuary. First, he praised my drawings. Second, he took them away. Third, he locked me out." She points at a sign on the gate: "NO ARCHITECTS."

"What's he really building up there?" asks Indi, sketching the cranes.

"Whatever it is, he won't come up here to check on it," says Wren. "He hates the cold. He sends drones instead."

The Architect looks at her over the top of the blueprint. Wren shrugs. "Lucky guess."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

The Architect unrolls her blueprint, studies it for a long moment, then rolls it up again. "First, win my badge. Second, then we will talk. In conclusion, not yet."

Just then, Girderoo pricks up his ears. Something behind the gold fence has caught his eye, and he bounds up the scaffold to peek through the bars.

A gold MaxxCam drone hums out of the clouds above him, and Maxx's voice crackles from its speaker.

"A wallaby in a hard hat? He's already dressed for Maxx World! That's Maxx-imum content, Vantafam. Bag him!"

A net drops. Girderoo is gone before anyone can move.

The Architect opens her mouth to speak. For the first time since you met her, her words come out in no order at all.

"Girderoo... the net... they... my wallaby."
